model_annotation: This figure presents a nested donut chart (also referred to as a concentric ring chart) illustrating the distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The chart contains two concentric rings with a total of seven distinct categories across both rings. The outer ring represents Ambiguity Std and is divided into four slices: Std: 0.0 shown in a dark teal/green color occupying approximately 47.7% of the ring, Std: 0.47 shown in a reddish/coral color at approximately 19.0%, Std: 0.82 shown in a gold/yellow color at approximately 5.0%, and Std: 0.94 shown in a light blue color at approximately 7.0%. The remaining portion of the outer ring (approximately 21.3%) appears to correspond to unlabeled space or overlap with adjacent segments. The inner ring represents Max Ambiguity and is divided into three slices: Max: 1 shown in a dark navy/blue color at approximately 38.0%, Max: 2 shown in a medium blue color at approximately 39.0%, and Max: 3 shown in a light blue color at approximately 14.2%. Percentage labels are displayed directly on or adjacent to each slice within both rings. A legend is provided to the right of the chart, separately listing the color codes for the outer ring (Ambiguity Std) and the inner ring (Max Ambiguity). The slices in the outer ring appear ordered with the largest segment (Std: 0.0 at 47.7%) being the most prominent, while in the inner ring, Max: 2 (39.0%) and Max: 1 (38.0%) are nearly equal in size, with Max: 3 (14.2%) being the smallest.
